scope: United States Capitol, Washington DC (detailed schematic)
title: United States Capitol
blurb: The seat of the United States Congress on Capitol Hill: 751 ft long, crowned by Thomas U. Walter’s 288 ft cast-iron dome and the bronze Statue of Freedom, with the Senate wing to the north and the House wing to the south.

sourceUrls.label: Architect of the Capitol: Rotunda restoration
Architect of the Capitol: Frederick Law Olmsted

systems.name: Dome
systems.description: Thomas U. Walter’s cast-iron dome, 288 ft tall and 96 ft in diameter, built 1855 to 1866: drum, peristyle colonnade, ribs, lantern and the Statue of Freedom.

systems.name: Rotunda
systems.description: The 96 ft circular hall beneath the dome, built 1818 to 1824: walls, frieze, history paintings and Brumidi’s Apotheosis of Washington in the canopy.

systems.name: Central Block
systems.description: The original central building from Thornton’s 1793 design: Statuary Hall, the old chambers and the East Front extension.

systems.name: Senate Wing
systems.description: The north wing of Walter’s 1850s extension, in Lee marble: the Senate chamber, floor 80 by 113 ft, in use since January 4, 1859.

systems.name: House Wing
systems.description: The south wing of Walter’s 1850s extension, in Lee marble: the House chamber in use since 1857.

systems.name: Porticos
systems.description: The columned porticos and pediments of the east and west fronts and the wing ends (column counts schematic).

systems.name: Crypt and Ground Floor
systems.description: The circular crypt beneath the rotunda with its 40 Doric sandstone columns, Washington’s Tomb and the foundation.

systems.name: Corridors and Stairs
systems.description: Connector corridors, grand stairs and the underground Capitol Visitor Center.

systems.name: Terraces
systems.description: Frederick Law Olmsted’s marble terraces on the north, west and south sides, completed 1892.

systems.name: Grounds
systems.description: Olmsted’s landscaped grounds: lawns, paths, trees, the 1879 to 1881 summerhouse and the Reflecting Pool (layout schematic).

systems.name: Ornament and Flags
systems.description: Pediment sculpture, bronze doors, the 1851 cornerstone and the chamber flags that fly when each house sits.

explanations.dome drum: The drum carrying Walter’s cast-iron dome, ringed by the peristyle colonnade. The dome is 288 ft tall and 96 ft in diameter, built 1855 to 1866, and is really two domes, one inside the other. Exact drum profile is schematic.
explanations.dome peristyle columns: Thirty-six hollow cast-iron Corinthian columns around the base of the dome, supplied by Poole and Hunt of Baltimore. They are purely decorative and carry none of the dome’s weight. Positions are schematic.
explanations.dome entablature: The entablature crowning the peristyle, doubling as flues and rain leaders for the rooms below. Exact profile is schematic.
explanations.dome ribs: The cast-iron ribs that carry the dome’s shell, the inner shell with the Apotheosis of Washington, and the tholos. The frame was built by Janes, Fowler, Kirtland and Co. of the Bronx. Exact rib curvature is schematic.
explanations.dome shell: The outer cast-iron shell of the dome, made of fish-scaled overlapping plates painted to look like the stone of the building below. Exact surface is schematic.
explanations.dome windows: A selection of the 108 windows in the dome, lighting the rotunda from the drum. Exact window layout is schematic.
explanations.dome base cornice: Cornice at the foot of the dome drum, spreading its visual weight onto the rotunda walls. Exact profile is schematic.
explanations.dome lantern drum: The tholos, the small lantern temple above the dome that carries the Statue of Freedom. Dimensions are schematic.
explanations.lantern colonnade: The colonnade ringing the tholos lantern. Column count is schematic.
explanations.lantern cap: The cap over the lantern, the last ironwork before the statue’s pedestal. Exact profile is schematic.
explanations.freedom pedestal: The cast-iron pedestal and globe on which the Statue of Freedom stands. Exact shape is schematic.
explanations.statue of freedom: The 19.5 ft bronze Statue of Freedom by Thomas Crawford, weighing about 15,000 lb: a female allegorical figure with a sheathed sword, laurel wreath and shield. Cast in five sections by Clark Mills in 1860 to 1862 with the help of the enslaved Philip Reid, and raised on December 2, 1863 to a 35-gun salute. This figure is a stylized schematic.
explanations.rotunda drum wall: The circular sandstone wall of the rotunda, 96 ft across, rising through the central block to carry the dome. Built 1818 to 1824 under Charles Bulfinch from William Thornton’s 1793 design. Exact wall treatment is schematic.
explanations.rotunda cornice: Cornice crowning the rotunda drum where the dome’s peristyle begins. Exact profile is schematic.
explanations.rotunda interior wall: The curved interior wall of the rotunda, rising 48 ft above the floor to the top of Bulfinch’s original walls. Exact surface is schematic.
explanations.rotunda floor: The second-floor level of the rotunda, the ceremonial heart of the Capitol where honored dead lie in state. Exact floor pattern is schematic.
explanations.rotunda pilasters: Fluted Doric pilasters dividing the curved rotunda wall, a schematic rendering of Bulfinch’s neoclassical detail.
explanations.rotunda frieze: The Frieze of American History circling the rotunda wall. Exact artwork is schematic.
explanations.rotunda history paintings: Four of the large history paintings hung in the rotunda, including Trumbull’s Declaration of Independence, Surrender of Lord Cornwallis and Washington Resigning His Commission. Frames and positions are schematic.
explanations.apotheosis of washington: Constantino Brumidi’s fresco of the Apotheosis of Washington, completed in 1866 in the oculus at the top of the inner dome, 180 ft above the rotunda floor. This disc is a schematic marker.
explanations.rotunda inner dome: The inner of Walter’s two domes, seen from the rotunda floor rising to the canopy. Exact profile is schematic.
explanations.rotunda doors: The four doorways of the rotunda, opening north to the Senate, south to the House, east to the front and west to the terraces. Exact door design is schematic.
explanations.rotunda east stair: Staircase rising to the rotunda floor on the east side. Exact stair layout is schematic.
explanations.rotunda west stair: Staircase rising to the rotunda floor on the west side. Exact stair layout is schematic.
explanations.central block: The original central building from Thornton’s 1793 competition design, 351 ft 7 1/2 in long before Walter’s extensions. Exact massing is schematic.
explanations.central block roof: Roof slab of the central block carrying the dome drum. Exact construction is schematic.
explanations.central block cornice: Cornice banding the central block below the roofline. Exact profile is schematic.
explanations.national statuary hall: The semi-circular National Statuary Hall immediately south of the rotunda, the House of Representatives chamber until 1857. Exact room shape is schematic.
explanations.statuary hall statues: A selection of the 35 statues of the National Statuary Hall Collection now displayed in the hall. Figures and positions are schematic.
explanations.old senate chamber: The Old Senate Chamber northeast of the rotunda, used by the Senate until 1859 and then by the Supreme Court until 1935. Interior is schematic.
explanations.old supreme court chamber: The chamber below the old Senate room that housed the Supreme Court in the early 1800s. Interior is schematic.
explanations.central block east windows: Window bays of the central block’s east front. Exact fenestration is schematic.
explanations.central block west windows: Window bays of the central block’s west front. Exact fenestration is schematic.
explanations.east front extension: The mid-20th-century marble extension of the East Front, built after the original 1828 sandstone portico columns were removed to the National Arboretum. Exact massing is schematic.
explanations.central block vaults: Vaulted basement spaces of the central block. Interior is schematic.
explanations.central block doors: The east and west entrance doors of the central block. Exact door design is schematic.
explanations.senate wing: The north wing of Walter’s 1850s extension, faced in Lee, Massachusetts marble with Cockeysville marble columns, more than doubling the building’s length. Exact massing is schematic.
explanations.senate wing roof: Roof slab of the Senate wing. Exact construction is schematic.
explanations.senate wing cornice: Cornice banding the Senate wing. Exact profile is schematic.
explanations.senate chamber: The Senate chamber in the north wing, designed by Walter: a two-story room whose floor is 80 by 113 ft, in use since January 4, 1859. Interior detail is schematic.
explanations.senate desks: The 100 senators’ desks on a tiered semicircular platform facing the rostrum. Arrangement is schematic.
explanations.senate rostrum: The rostrum at the front of the Senate chamber. Exact form is schematic.
explanations.senate gallery: The second-floor gallery overlooking the Senate floor on all four sides. Exact layout is schematic.
explanations.senate wing north windows: Window bays of the Senate wing’s north end. Exact fenestration is schematic.
explanations.senate wing east windows: Window bays of the Senate wing’s east side. Exact fenestration is schematic.
explanations.senate wing west windows: Window bays of the Senate wing’s west side. Exact fenestration is schematic.
explanations.senate reception room: The Senate Reception Room adjoining the chamber. Interior is schematic.
explanations.house wing: The south wing of Walter’s 1850s extension, faced in Lee, Massachusetts marble. Exact massing is schematic.
explanations.house wing roof: Roof slab of the House wing. Exact construction is schematic.
explanations.house wing cornice: Cornice banding the House wing. Exact profile is schematic.
explanations.house chamber: The House chamber in the south wing, in use since 1857 when the House left Statuary Hall. Dimensions and interior are schematic.
explanations.house desks: The 435 representatives’ desks in tiered arcs facing the rostrum. Arrangement is schematic.
explanations.house rostrum: The Speaker’s rostrum at the front of the House chamber. Exact form is schematic.
explanations.house gallery: The second-floor gallery overlooking the House floor. Exact layout is schematic.
explanations.house wing south windows: Window bays of the House wing’s south end. Exact fenestration is schematic.
explanations.house wing east windows: Window bays of the House wing’s east side. Exact fenestration is schematic.
explanations.house wing west windows: Window bays of the House wing’s west side. Exact fenestration is schematic.
explanations.speaker’s lobby: The Speaker’s Lobby behind the House rostrum. Interior is schematic.

explanations.west portico: The columned West Portico facing the National Mall. Column count and positions are schematic.

explanations.crypt vault ceiling: The groined vaulting over the crypt that carries the rotunda floor. Exact vaulting is schematic.
explanations.washington’s tomb: The empty burial chamber two stories below the rotunda, built into Thornton’s original design to entomb George Washington and never used. Interior is schematic.
explanations.compass stone: A white marble compass stone in the crypt floor marking the point where Washington, D.C.’s four quadrants meet. Exact marker is schematic.
explanations.crypt statues: Thirteen statues of the National Statuary Hall Collection displayed in the crypt. Figures and positions are schematic.
explanations.foundation slab: The foundation carrying the Capitol’s 175,170 sq ft footprint. Exact extent is schematic.
